mainTopic: End of פרק האשה: checking a בית הפרס for people bringing the קרבן פסח. Start of פרק מי שהיה טמא: who brings פסח שני, and why the Torah mentions טמא and דרך רחוקה specifically.
overview: This עמוד opens with the end of a ruling: we check a בית הפרס (a field that may hold crushed bones) for people bringing the קרבן פסח, but not for people eating תרומה. שמואל explains that the check is done by blowing on the dust while walking. A second view says that a trampled בית הפרס is simply טהור. Then פרק האשה closes with the הדרן, and פרק מי שהיה טמא begins. Its משנה teaches that a טמא, someone on a דרך רחוקה, a שוגג, and an אנוס all bring פסח שני. The תורה names טמא and דרך רחוקה only to show who is פטור from כרת. The גמרא then brings a מחלוקת about a far-away person whose פסח was brought for him anyway. רב נחמן says it counts and רב ששת says it does not, and each side argues from the wording 'ולא עשה' and the plural 'חייבין' in the משנה. Finally רב ששת begins quoting a ברייתא of רבי עקיבא, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Checking a field of crushed bones for פסח but not for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a cited source. It rules that we check a בית הפרס for people bringing the קרבן פסח, but not for people eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...that we check [a בית הפרס] for those making the פסח, but we do not check for those eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The text finishes a ruling from the previous discussion. It says the רבנן allow a special check of a בית הפרס so that people can stay טהור for the קרבן פסח, but they do not allow it for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of a בית הפרס is only a rabbinic decree. For פסח, missing the קרבן carries כרת, so the רבנן allowed a check to help people. For תרומה, the stakes are lower, so they did not relax the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: we check / examine
people bringing the קרבן פסח
people eating תרומה (the כהן's portion)
a field where a grave was plowed up, so it may hold small bone pieces (rabbinic טומאה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common principle: the רבנן sometimes relax their own decrees when a Torah obligation with כרת is at stake.

phrases.english: that we check for those making the Pesach,
phrases.notes: Referring to a בית הפרס on the way to ירושלים.

phrases.english: but we do not check for those eating terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes a source cited at the end of the previous discussion (on the previous amud).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית הפרס may be checked to allow people to bring the קרבן פסח, but not to allow people to eat תרומה.

steps.title: How is the checking done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this 'checking' actually involves in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'we check (for those making the פסח)' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about how the check works. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the ruling. It asks for a definition of the procedure, because a field full of dust and possible bone pieces is not obviously something you can check.

keyTerms.meaning: what? (what does it mean?)

phrases.english: What is meant by 'we check (for those making the Pesach)'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical meaning of the ruling in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method of checking a בית הפרס.

steps.title: שמואל: blow on the dust while walking
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, says the person blows on the dust in front of him as he walks through the בית הפרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: He blows [on the dust of] the בית הפרס as he walks along.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. The person walks slowly and blows away the dust in front of each step to see whether any bone is hidden there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns 'checking' into a real physical search. If he finds no bone where he steps, he has not touched טומאה, and he stays טהור for the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: blows (on the dust)
and continues walking (does this as he goes)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
He blows on the beit haperas as he walks along.
phrases.notes: He blows the dust before each step to uncover any hidden bone.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The check is done by blowing away the dust ahead of each step while walking through.

steps.title: A trampled field of crushed bones is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אביי, quoting רב יהודה, says that a בית הפרס that people have trampled is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אביי said in the name of רב יהודה: A בית הפרס that has been trampled is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report from רב יהודה gives a different way to deal with a בית הפרס. If the path has already been trampled by people walking on it, it is simply treated as pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no personal check is needed. We assume that heavy foot traffic has already moved or crushed any bone pieces too small to matter. This is another way the rabbinic decree is relaxed.

keyTerms.meaning: in the name of
that was trampled / trodden down
ritually pure

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to pass through a בית הפרס for פסח. One is blowing on the dust as you walk (שמואל). The other is that a trampled path is already טהור (רב יהודה בר אביי quoting רב יהודה).

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַבָּיֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Abaye said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
A beit haperas that has been trampled is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַבָּיֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different report of how a בית הפרס can be treated as pure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A trampled בית הפרס is טהור.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק האשה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the eighth פרק of פסחים, פרק האשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, [פרק] האשה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of פרק האשה. It is a traditional closing statement, not part of the legal argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן expresses the learner's wish to come back and learn this פרק again. Nothing in the argument changes here. It only marks a boundary before a new פרק begins.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (closing formula of a perek)

phrases.english: We will return to you, [the chapter] HaIsha

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק that the previous steps ended.

steps.title: An impure person or a far-away traveler brings פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The new perek opens. Someone who was טמא or on a דרך רחוקה and did not bring the first פסח must bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who was טמא or on a distant journey and did not make the first [פסח] should make the second [פסח].
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens פרק ט with the basic rule of פסח שני. It starts with the two cases the תורה itself names: someone who was impure and someone who was far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the two cases written in the תורה (במדבר ט). They missed the 14th of ניסן, so they bring the קרבן on the 14th of אייר.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (marks the start of a משנה)
ritually impure
a distant journey
the first פסח (14 ניסן) / the second פסח (14 אייר)

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who was impure
or on a distant journey
and did not make the first [Pesach] —
should make the second [Pesach].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new perek with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא or a traveler on a דרך רחוקה who missed the first פסח brings פסח שני.

steps.title: Also someone who forgot or was held back
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that someone who missed the first פסח by mistake (שוגג) or by circumstances beyond his control (אונס) also brings פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he erred or was prevented, and did not make the first, he should make the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the rule of פסח שני beyond the two cases the תורה names. Anyone who missed the first פסח, whether by mistake or because he was forced, brings the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This addition creates a puzzle. If people the תורה does not mention also bring פסח שני, why does the תורה name only טמא and דרך רחוקה? The next step asks exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: acted by mistake / forgot
was forced / prevented by circumstances beyond his control

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think פסח שני is only for the טמא and the traveler. The משנה says that anyone who missed the first פסח brings the second. The difference between the groups is about כרת, as the next steps explain.

phrases.english: If he erred unwittingly or was prevented by circumstance
and did not make the first [Pesach] —
should make the second [Pesach].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of Step 6 to more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שוגג or an אנוס who missed the first פסח also brings פסח שני.

steps.title: Then why does the תורה mention only impure and far away?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: if everyone who missed the first פסח brings the second, why does the פסוק name only טמא and דרך רחוקה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why is it said [in the תורה] 'impure' or 'was on a distant journey'?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה itself raises a question about the פסוק. It is setting up its own answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question points to a problem: the תורה's naming of two specific cases seems unnecessary if the rule covers everyone. That means the two named cases must teach something special.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
why was it stated (in the פסוק)?

phrases.english: If so, why is it stated
'impure' or 'one who was on a distant journey'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the פסוק in light of the wider rule given in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the Torah teaches by naming only טמא and דרך רחוקה.

steps.title: The difference is about כרת
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the two named groups are פטור from כרת, while the others are חייב כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It teaches] that these are exempt from כרת, and those are liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. Everyone brings פסח שני, but the תורה names טמא and דרך רחוקה to show that these groups are not punished with כרת, while other groups can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the special mention in the תורה concerns punishment, not who brings פסח שני. Exactly who is פטור and who is חייב, and in which situation, is explained in the coming גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: exempt
liable
spiritual 'cutting off', the punishment for not bringing the קרבן פסח

steps.whatToRemember: פסח שני is for everyone who missed the first פסח. The תורה names טמא and דרך רחוקה only to teach that those two groups are פטור from כרת, while others are חייב כרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the framework for the whole פרק: who brings פסח שני, and how missing the פסח relates to the punishment of כרת.

phrases.english: that these are exempt from karet,
and those are liable to karet.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah names טמא and דרך רחוקה to exempt them from כרת, unlike others, who are liable to כרת.

steps.title: The dispute: a far-away person whose פסח was brought anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presents a מחלוקת. A person on a דרך רחוקה had his פסח שחט'd and its blood sprinkled for him. רב נחמן says it is accepted. רב ששת says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated: A person was on a far-away journey, yet the פסח was slaughtered and its blood sprinkled for him. רב נחמן said: it is accepted. רב ששת said: it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה with a new case that the משנה did not address. Two אמוראים argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה told us that a person on a דרך רחוקה brings פסח שני. It did not say what happens if his פסח ראשון was brought for him anyway. The question is whether that offering counts, so that he no longer needs פסח שני. רב נחמן says yes and רב ששת says no.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces a dispute between אמוראים
A far-away journey that keeps a person from the עזרה on ערב פסח
And they sprinkled the blood on his behalf
He has been accepted: the קרבן counts and he has fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion on the משנה.

phrases.english: It was stated: If one was on a far-away journey
and they slaughtered it and sprinkled its blood for him,
phrases.notes: Others in ירושלים brought his פסח on his behalf.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: He has been accepted.
Rav Sheshet said: He has not been accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's case of דרך רחוקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: the קרבן counts. רב ששת: the קרבן does not count.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reasoning: the תורה went easy on him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the exemption for a דרך רחוקה is a kindness, not a disqualification. If he does bring it, he deserves a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said it is accepted, because the Merciful One showed pity on him. And if he does do it, may a blessing come upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב נחמן holds the קרבן counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that the person on a דרך רחוקה is fully fit to bring the פסח. The תורה simply spared him the trouble of traveling. Since he is not disqualified, a פסח brought for him is fully valid and even praiseworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה (literally 'the Merciful One') took pity on him: the exemption is a leniency
May a blessing come upon him: he did something good

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: He has been accepted,
because the Merciful One took pity on him.
phrases.notes: The exemption exists only to spare him, not to push him out.

phrases.english: And if he does do it —
may a blessing come upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הוּרְצָה, מֵיחָס הוּא דְּחַס רַחֲמָנָא עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב נחמן's position from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The דרך רחוקה exemption is a leniency, so a פסח brought anyway is valid.

steps.title: רב ששת's reasoning: the תורה pushed him off like a טמא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the תורה pushed the far-away person out of the first פסח, exactly like a טמא, so his offering does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said it is not accepted, because the Merciful One pushed him off, like a טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב ששת holds the קרבן does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת reads the פסוק as putting דרך רחוקה in the same group as טמא. The תורה treats both as removed from the first פסח, so his time to bring it is פסח שני. A פסח brought for him on the first date is therefore not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה pushed him off: he is disqualified from the first פסח
Like a person who is ritually impure

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said: He has not been accepted,
because the Merciful One pushed him off, like an impure person.
phrases.notes: The פסוק mentions דרך רחוקה alongside טמא, so they share one status.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: לֹא הוּרְצָה, מִידְחֵא דַּחְיֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא כְּטָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning, parallel to step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דרך רחוקה is a disqualification like טמאה, so a פסח brought anyway is invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core question of the whole סוגיא. Is an exemption a 'gift of leniency' or a 'removal from the מצוה'? The answer decides whether doing it anyway is a ברכה or worthless.

steps.title: רב נחמן's proof from the words 'and did not do the first'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites our משנה, which says the far-away person 'did not do' the first פסח. That wording implies he could have done it if he wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: From where do I say this? As we learned: One who was טמא or on a far-away journey and did not do the first, should do the second. This implies that if he wanted, he could have done it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a proof for his view from the wording of the משנה we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have said simply 'a טמא or far-away person brings פסח שני.' Instead it adds 'and did not do the first.' רב נחמן reads that extra phrase as hinting that doing the first was an option. If it was an option, it would count if he did it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? Introduces a speaker's own proof
As we learned in a משנה
And he did not do the first פסח
By implication: if he wanted, he could have done it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: From where do I say it?
As we learned: One who was impure
or on a far-away journey
and did not do the first —
should do the second.
This implies that if he wanted, he could have done it.
phrases.notes: This applies at least to the far-away person, since a טמא truly cannot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's reasoning from step 11 with a textual source.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that a far-away person's פסח counts if brought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's extra phrase 'ולא עשה את הראשון', which implies doing it was an option.

steps.title: רב ששת: the same words appear where 'he could have' is impossible
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת points out that the סיפא uses the identical phrase 'and did not do' for שוגג and אונס. Those people clearly could not have done it, so the phrase cannot mean 'he could have done it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת would tell you: If so, the סיפא teaches: one who acted by mistake or was forced and did not do the first should do the second. Since it says 'and did not do', that should imply that if he wanted, he could have done it. But he made a mistake, and he was forced!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת rejects רב נחמן's proof by showing that the same reasoning leads to nonsense in the next line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ולא עשה' really means 'he could have done it if he wanted,' then the סיפא would say that about a שוגג and an אונס. But a person who forgot, or was blocked by circumstances, by definition could not choose to do it. So the phrase cannot carry the meaning רב נחמן gave it.

keyTerms.meaning: And רב ששת would answer you: introduces the other side's response
If so: if your reasoning were correct
The latter clause of the משנה
But look, he acted by mistake, and look, he was forced

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet would say to you:
If so, the latter clause, which teaches:
If one acted by mistake or was forced
and did not do the first —
he should do the second.
Since it teaches 'and did not do,'
that would imply that if he wanted, he could have done it.
But he acted by mistake, and he was forced!
phrases.notes: Such people could not have chosen to do it, so the inference fails.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר לָךְ: אִי הָכִי, סֵיפָא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רב נחמן's proof from the wording, not necessarily his ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'ולא עשה' also appears for שוגג and אונס, where 'he could have done it' is impossible. So the phrase cannot imply choice.

steps.title: The real meaning: an extra case hidden in each clause
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains 'ולא עשה' differently. In the סיפא it adds a מזיד alongside שוגג and אונס. In the רישא it adds an אונן alongside טמא and דרך רחוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is teaching an intentional sinner together with them. Here too, it is teaching an אונן together with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his rejection by offering his own reading of the phrase 'and did not do.' This removes רב נחמן's proof completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, 'ולא עשה' adds a person who simply chose not to bring the פסח (a מזיד). He too brings פסח שני. By the same pattern, in the רישא the phrase adds an אונן, a mourner whose relative died that day, to the list alongside טמא and דרך רחוקה. So the phrase marks an extra category in each clause. It does not mean the far-away person 'could have done it.'

keyTerms.meaning: One who intentionally did not bring the פסח
It teaches it together with them: an unstated case included alongside the listed ones
Here too: applying the same pattern to the other clause
A mourner on the day of a close relative's death, before burial

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches an intentional one together with them.
phrases.notes: In the סיפא, 'ולא עשה' includes someone who skipped the first פסח on purpose.

phrases.english: Here too: it teaches an acute mourner together with them.
phrases.notes: In the רישא, 'ולא עשה' includes an אונן alongside טמא and דרך רחוקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's rejection by giving the correct meaning of 'ולא עשה'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's wording: the phrase adds an unlisted category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ולא עשה' implies the far-away person could have brought the first פסח, so it would count.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ולא עשה' adds a מזיד in the סיפא and an אונן in the רישא. No proof for רב נחמן remains.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the אונן is added to the סיפא. The מזיד belongs to the סיפא (with שוגג and אונס). The אונן belongs to the רישא (with טמא and דרך רחוקה).
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן tried to prove from 'ולא עשה' that the far-away person had a choice. רב ששת showed the phrase actually adds an extra case in each clause: מזיד in the סיפא, אונן in the רישא. So the proof falls away.

steps.title: רב אשי: The plural 'they are liable' supports רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the משנה's plural 'חייבין' as covering two cases, the מזיד and the אונן. This supports רב ששת's view that 'ולא עשה' adds cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Our משנה is also precise this way, for it teaches: 'These are exempt from כרת, and these are liable to כרת.' Which cases does that refer to? If you say it refers to the שוגג and the נאנס, are a שוגג and a נאנס subject to כרת?! Rather, is it not referring to the מזיד and the אונן?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for רב ששת from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'these are liable to כרת' in the plural, so it must be talking about more than one person. The שוגג and נאנס cannot be the ones meant, because people who were careless by accident or forced never get כרת. So the plural must cover the two extra cases that רב ששת said 'ולא עשה' adds, the מזיד and the אונן.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is also precise this way (its wording supports the view)
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for not bringing the קרבן פסח on purpose
To which (case) does this refer?
If you say
Rather, is it not that

steps.confusionAlert: The proof hangs on the plural ending: 'חייבין' (plural) versus 'חייב' (singular). Watch for the plural, because רב נחמן's reply in the next step targets exactly this.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Our mishna is also precise (in support of Rav Sheshet),
for it teaches:
These are exempt from karet
and these are liable to karet.
phrases.notes: 'Liable' is plural, which implies more than one case.

phrases.english: To which cases does this refer?
If you say to the unwitting one and the coerced one,
are the unwitting and the coerced subject to karet?!
Rather, is it not referring to the intentional one and the acute mourner?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב ששת's reading from Step 15 that 'ולא עשה' adds the מזיד and the אונן.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's claim that the extra phrase 'ולא עשה' adds cases (the מזיד and the אונן) instead of showing that the far-away person had a choice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural 'חייבין בהכרת' in the משנה, which must refer to more than one liable person.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Only the intentional one is meant, and the plural is just style
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says 'חייבין' refers only to the מזיד. The plural form was chosen only to match the earlier plural 'פטורין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן would tell you: Really, it refers to the מזיד alone. By right the משנה should have said 'he is liable' (singular). It says 'they are liable' only because the first part said 'they are exempt' (plural), so the later part also used the plural.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects רב אשי's proof by explaining the plural word another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's proof needed the plural to mean two real cases. רב נחמן says the plural is only a matter of style: the משנה kept the same plural form as 'פטורין'. So only the מזיד is liable, the אונן is not added, and רב נחמן's reading of the רישא (the far-away person could have brought it) still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (I keep my original position)
By itself / alone
By right it should have been
Since the first part taught it this way (the later part copies its style)
The latter part of the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: The 'אַיְּידֵי' answer is a common גמרא tool. It explains that a word's form can come from matching nearby wording, so it is not always a precise legal signal.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman would say to you:
Actually, it refers to the intentional one alone.
And by right it should have
taught 'he is liable' (singular),
and the fact that it teaches 'they are liable' (plural)
is because the first clause taught 'they are exempt' (plural),
so the latter clause taught 'they are liable' (plural).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר לָךְ: לְעוֹלָם אַמֵּזִיד לְחוֹדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's proof from the plural in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the plural 'חייבין'. It does not disprove רב ששת's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plural is a matter of style, matching 'פטורין', and does not show two separate liable cases.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: the plural 'חייבין' means two cases (מזיד and אונן), which helps רב ששת. רב נחמן: only the מזיד is meant, and the plural just matches 'פטורין'.

steps.title: רב ששת begins quoting his source from רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת introduces a ברייתא of רבי עקיבא as the source for his view. It begins by noting that the תורה mentions both 'טמא' and 'בדרך רחוקה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: From where do I say this? As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא says, it says 'טמא' (impure), and it says 'בדרך רחוקה' (on a distant journey)...
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts bringing a source for his position. This line only sets up the ברייתא, and its point continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's view was that the far-away person is pushed out of the first פסח just like a טמא. The ברייתא opens by placing the two cases, טמא and דרך רחוקה, side by side in the פסוק. This prepares a comparison between them that the next lines will finish.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (I am bringing my source)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
It is stated (in the פסוק)
Ritually impure person
On a distant journey

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
From where do I say it?
As it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Akiva says:
It is stated 'impure,'
and it is stated 'on a distant journey,'
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was deflected in Step 17, רב ששת turns to a ברייתא for support.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view (Step 12) that the far-away person is pushed out of the first פסח like a טמא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי עקיבא comparing 'טמא' and 'בדרך רחוקה' (continued on the next amud).
